claims.text: SLM can fabricate Group IV-V refractory high-entropy alloys such as Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V.
A high scan speed and low hatch distance strategy induces cellular solidification.
Parameter Set B, characterized by low scan speed and a small melt pool, produces an almost cellular structure.
Laser scan speed, hatch distance, and melt-pool geometry control the G/R ratio and hence cellular versus dendritic solidification.
Rapid SLM solidification limits grain growth and produces fine grains and reduced dendrite-arm spacing.
Processing at 1200–1400 °C reduces the volume fraction of Laves phases.
Laves phases such as Cr2Nb and (Fe,Cr)Nb are brittle secondary phases that can impair mechanical performance.
Aging at 650 °C nucleates coherent δ-lamellae or γ″ stepwise controllable nanoprecipitates.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission, relieve stress concentrations, and inhibit premature microcrack initiation.
Coherent nanoprecipitates mitigate brittleness caused specifically by carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen interstitial impurities.
The proposed SLM, homogenization, and aging route yields a single-phase BCC matrix containing coherent nanoprecipitates.
Annealing reduces Laves phases by reducing atomic-radius misfit and elastic energy.
Maintaining VEC below 4.4 ensures single-phase BCC stability and enhanced mechanical performance.
The proposed route enhances room-temperature ductility.
The proposed alloy will retain high-temperature structural integrity through improved creep resistance.
The proposed alloy will retain high-temperature structural integrity through improved oxidation resistance.
The proposed alloy will achieve tensile strain greater than 14% at 800 °C without microcrack formation.
Conventionally cast NbMoTaW-type RHEAs have approximately 200 μm grains, compared with much finer SLM microstructures.
SLM-processed RHEAs without post-annealing retain high dislocation densities and are susceptible to cracking.
Ti-containing NbMoTaWV-based systems may undergo an FCC-to-monoclinic instability at ambient temperature if cooling is not controlled.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes cellular solidification to high scan speed, whereas the intervention also identifies low-scan-speed Parameter Set B as the cellular condition. The cited comparison reports high-speed Parameter Set A as coarser and dendritic and low-speed Parameter Set B as almost cellular.

The final state is called single-phase BCC while also being described as containing δ/γ″ nanoprecipitates. If the precipitates are compositionally or structurally distinct phases, the overall microstructure is not strictly single-phase.

The mechanism says reduced atomic-radius misfit and elastic energy cause Laves-phase reduction during annealing, but the cited mechanism states that Laves precipitation itself reduces the solid-solution misfit and elastic energy.
